group: bouncer with a counter in a fixed wall
title: What is known about 1RB---_1LC0RF_1LD0LC_0RE0LF_0RD1LA_1RB0LE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB---_1LC0RF_1LD0LC_0RE0LF_0RD1LA_1RB0LE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The head bounces between a block that grows at the left end and a wall of exactly 1,573 cells at the right end that it rewrites every sweep like a counter; the counter would need something like 348 sweeps to fill the wall, and what happens then is the question.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (A1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 34,610 cells have been visited and 20,724 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.494). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: A wall of fixed length that counts
claims.text: After 2·107 steps the tape at each sweep is C>0 (01101)^n W with W exactly 1,573 cells and n growing by one per four sweeps. Consecutive walls differ from cell 44 on; the deepest change reaches cells 252, 294, 319, 344, 369 at sweeps 274, 406, 2,296, 7,335, 20,772 (by 1010 steps).

claims.title: A wall of fixed length that counts
claims.text: After 2·107 steps the tape at each sweep is C>0 (01101)^n W with W exactly 1,573 cells and n growing by about one per sweep. Consecutive walls differ from cell 44 on; the deepest change reaches cells 252, 294, 319, 344, 369 at sweeps 274, 406, 2,296, 7,335, 20,772 (by 1010 steps).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The decider pipeline of bbchallenge left it open; no proof either way is recorded here yet.

sections.heading: A counter inside a fixed wall
html: The left part of the tape is the word 01101 repeated, about one more copy per sweep. The right part is a wall that has had exactly 1,573 cells since 2·107 steps: the right end of the tape never moves.

The wall is different after every sweep, but not at random. Comparing one wall with the next, the changes always start at the same cell, 44, and usually stay within a hundred cells; only now and then do they reach further, and each new depth (25 cells further each time) is reached about three times later than the previous one. That is how the carries of a counter behave: digits about 25 cells wide, in a base near 3.

About 48 such digits are left before the carries reach the end of the wall, which would take something like 348 sweeps. Whether the machine then halts or makes room is the open question; decoding the digits would make it exact.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.494). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 34,610 cells (25,368 left of the start, 201 right), with a density of 1s of 0.599.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: A bouncer between a growing block and a wall of exactly 1,573 cells that changes every sweep like a counter (changes start at cell 44, carries reach 25 cells further about every three times as many sweeps); what happens when the carries reach the end of the wall is unknown.
